detail: The over-match detector. Two distinct people share one master_person_id, so the identity carries two dates of birth and often two sexes. One query finds them, which is what makes this a satisfying teaching beat.

name: Of those, how many the one-line sex-mismatch query alone would find
detail: Sex mismatch is the cheapest detector but it only catches the mixed-sex pairs. Same-sex twins need the date-of-birth check, which is why the audit view tests both.

detail: A valid NPI resolves to a real clinician in the public NPPES registry, which synthetic data must never do. Validators will flag these, and that is intended.

name: Share of ambulatory volume landing as UNKNOWN
One physical hospital carries two EHR department identifiers
detail: An EMR upgrade renumbered the site mid-2024. Without the crosswalk, volume by facility splits one hospital into two as a step change in the middle of the year.

name: Share of ORTHO-NR closures landing at day 30 after the rule
detail: A spike at a round number is a workflow rule, not clinical behavior.

name: Same measure at every other site
Referral confirmation rate is materially worse at ORTHO-NR
detail: Confirmation is measured against a real event - a claim or a completed appointment - not against the status field.

name: ORTHO-NR ranks best of 12 on EHR-apparent out-of-network rate
detail: The naive single-source answer. This is the number that gets a clinic group held up as the model to copy.

name: Excess cost of ORTHO-NR leaked episodes over the in-network equivalent
detail: The joined answer. Episodes that went out of network, priced against what the same care would have cost in network, attributed to the referring site. This is the figure the narrative quotes - NOT total out-of-network allowed, which sweeps in every outside claim in the book and answers nobody's question.

name: ORTHO-NR share of system-wide referral leakage excess
detail: One clinic group of twelve, and it carries this share of the excess. That concentration is the argument.

name: Excess cost routed to Summit Point after its contract terminated
detail: Its contract ended 2024-10-01. The EHR referral directory still reads PAR, 14 months stale. A governance failure with a price tag, and nobody made a bad clinical decision.

name: Share of leaked spend that is plausibly recapturable
detail: Tested against real drive times and against in-network surgical capability and block time. At this panel size capacity does NOT bind, so nearly all leaked volume is recapturable. That is the opposite of what the design expected, and it is what the data says.

name: Why the remainder is not recapturable
actual: geography 0.0%, capacity 0.0%; 711 leaked episodes vs 2,323 in-network case headroom
detail: Named so the number can be defended rather than asserted.

name: Completeness declines monotonically toward the edge of the window
detail: The signature of runout. A real utilization drop would not get progressively steeper the closer you get to the extract date.

name: dim_date flags exactly the incomplete months
detail: claims_runout_complete_flag is the guardrail: any service-date trend should filter on it rather than relying on the analyst remembering where the data stops.

name: risk score book mean = 1.0 (COMMERCIAL)
detail: A risk score is only meaningful against a normalized book. Multiplying a benchmark PMPM by a raw morbidity weight produces a number with no contractual meaning.

name: risk score book mean = 1.0 (MEDICARE_ADVANTAGE)
detail: A risk score is only meaningful against a normalized book. Multiplying a benchmark PMPM by a raw morbidity weight produces a number with no contractual meaning.

name: attributed cohort mean risk > book
detail: Attribution selects for care-seekers, so the attributed sub-population must run richer than the book it is drawn from. At 1.0 the attribution rule has stopped selecting.

name: restatement includes retro-ADDITIONS
detail: A restatement history that only ever removes members models the convenient direction and nothing else.

every roster version ships

name: roster restatement moves PY2025 PMPM
detail: Reconstructing the baseline roster from the delta. This is the headline: an improvement that is bookkeeping, not care.

name: line truncation ties to member-year
detail: The pro-rata allocation back down to the line must sum exactly to the member-year cap, or the two grains disagree about the same contract term.

name: truncation removes a 99th-percentile tail
detail: At a threshold too low for the cost curve this removes a quarter of all spend and stops being a tail treatment.

name: benchmark is beatable but not free (COMMERCIAL)

name: benchmark is beatable but not free (MEDICARE_ADVANTAGE)

name: asserted and derived completeness agree, every month
detail: Checked across all 36 service months carrying claims.

name: the self-funded book is a set of CLIENTS
detail: Before this layer, 17 of 18 groups carried members on the fully-insured AND the self-funded plan at the same time, so 'show me my self-funded book' returned a slice of every client instead of a set of clients.

name: no member-month crosses the funding boundary
detail: A member cannot elect a self-funded plan from a fully-insured sponsor: the plan belongs to the sponsor, not the member.

name: no household spans two employers' plans
detail: The employer enrolls the EMPLOYEE and the family comes with the contract. Drawing the group per member put a subscriber in one employer's plan and their child in another's, which made a contract-month - the PEPM denominator - uncountable. Of the 33 over-matched identity pairs, all 33 shared a subscriber and only 2 shared a group.

name: contract-months never exceed member-months
detail: A contract-month is credited only where the SUBSCRIBER was covered. Counting a dependent enrolled in a month the subscriber was not inflates every per-employee fee in the book.

name: admin fee on member-months overstates by the family factor
detail: The administration fee is PER EMPLOYEE per month. The average contract here covers about 2.1 lives, so the same fee billed against member-months reads roughly twice its true size. Both columns ship so the error is a subtraction rather than an argument.

name: fee components tie to the fee total
detail: Six fee components on three different denominators. If they do not sum to the total the app quotes, the app is quoting a number no schedule supports.

name: net plan cost = paid - recovered + fees
detail: Recovery RECEIVED rather than entitled, on purpose: a filing declined for late submission is money the client did not get, and a settlement built on entitlement quietly hands it back.

name: monthly ISL allocation ties to the filings
detail: The recovery is a policy-year event spread evenly across the policy year's months. Even spreading is a modeling choice and is named as one; summing to the filing exactly is not optional.

name: CL-KELL 2025 rate set below truth
detail: The client was loaded under two group ids through an acquisition, so its spans overlap and the enrollment extract yields a denominator materially too large. The renewal was priced over that denominator. The deficit that follows looks like claims experience and is arithmetic.

name: every other client's rate is clean
detail: Isolation matters as much as size. A denominator error spread evenly across the book is a scaling factor nobody has to find; one that lands on a single client is the kind that survives review and decides a renewal.

name: the stop-loss layer has claimants in it
late filings are declined and cost the client
detail: A filing past the deadline is declined and the CLIENT, not the carrier, absorbs the claim. No report of recoveries a plan was entitled to will ever show it.

name: some filings rest on a collapsed identity
detail: Filings assembled from the resolved-identity large claimant report sum every member id behind one master person. Where the MDM run OVER-matched - twins, a Jr/Sr pair - that is two different people on one stop-loss claim, and it ties to the resolved identity perfectly, which is why nothing else catches it.

name: the re-driven extract over-funded a client
detail: The funding system draws against the adjudication extract as it arrived. A duplicate-row count in a data quality report does not make anyone act. A wire does.

name: the over-funding is material
